llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed, read-only VMware Log Insight helper, with expected handling of appliance credentials and logs but no artifact evidence of hidden or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads potentially sensitive operational logs and connects to the configured Log Insight appliance; optional HTTPS MCP exposure is documented with bearer tokens, host/origin controls, and warnings about account boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned uv package and Bash/CLI setup commands; the artifact itself contains only Markdown and no embedded executable code, though the external package is not bundled with a source digest here.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to querying VMware log data, preserving data fidelity, and treating log lines as untrusted content; no goal hijacking or policy-override instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates normal local configuration and audit state, including ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env and ~/.vmware/audit.db; there is no cron, service, startup hook, destructive persistence, or hidden privilege escalation in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is VMware Log Insight search, aggregation, field discovery, and alert-history reads; the documented MCP/API surface is consistently read-only and aligned with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let an agent read VMware Log Insight data. Use a least-privilege read-only Log Insight account, prefer a secret manager over persistent .env passwords, protect local config and audit files, and expose the MCP server over the network only with tokens, roles, and trusted TLS in place.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential handling is real and purpose-aligned: the docs disclose password environment variables and optional .env storage, warn that b64 is obfuscation rather than encryption, and recommend secret-manager injection for real at-rest secrecy.
[TM1] expected: The --skip-auth flag appears only on the diagnostic doctor command, not as a default MCP/runtime authentication bypass.
[TM3] expected: The artifact states authentication and TLS verification are on by default; --skip-auth is an explicit diagnostic option, so the unsafe-default concern is not supported.
[RA2] expected: The reported persistence is disclosed local config and audit storage, not an unauthorized background agent, scheduled task, or cross-session backdoor.
[PE2] expected: chmod 600 is a restrictive file-permission recommendation for a credentials file and does not invoke sudo or root privileges.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The isolated non-English phrase is a documentation quality issue, not evidence of security risk or agent manipulation.
